newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian wool indicator rises 1 cent to 707c/kg.
newsitem.headline: Australian wool indicator rises 1 cent to 707c/kg.

text.p: The Australian wool market eastern indicator rose one cent to 707 cents a kg clean on Tuesday at sales in Sydney and Melbourne, Wool International said.
Merino fleece was mixed, with 19/23 micron slightly cheaper, 20/24m 0.5 percent dearer, 21/22m unchanged, and 25/26m up to 1.5 percent dearer, while merino skirtings were fully firm.
In crossbreds, 27/28m were 0.5 percent dearer, and 29/30/31m slightly cheaper.
In cardings, lambs were slightly dearer, locks firm and crutchings generally unchanged.
WI said Japanese interests including China were principal buyers with good support from Western Europe.
Of the 31,509 bales offered, 8.5 percent were passed in.

In early Fremantle trading, merino fleece was cheaper, with 21m eight percent cheaper, 22/23m seven percent cheaper and 24m five percent cheaper, while merino skirtings were up to three percent cheaper.
Sales continue on Wednesday in Sydney, Melbourne and Fremantle with about 48,000 bales to be offered.
